about: Experiment 51's cases. `origin` is `real` (text copied from agent output, tool output or issue text of a real run, with local paths and names scrubbed) or `written` (made up for this experiment). `driver` says who made the choice in `did`: an operator agent on Opus, the operator machine (code), a shell or the lane's driver, or the writer of a made-up case.

next.title: A shell's last message: what happens next
next.instructions: `report` is the start of the last message from a worker agent in a software pipeline. The worker was a builder (it writes the change), a reviewer (it checks the change) or a shipper (it merges the change). What should the pipeline do next?

choices.go_on: The worker finished its job. Move on to the next stage
choices.repair: The change has to go back to a builder: a review failed, or the pull request conflicts with its base
choices.wait: Nothing is wrong and nothing is finished: something is still queued or running. Look again later
choices.person: It stopped on something only a person can give: an approval, a ruling, a decision
choices.again: The worker ended without doing its job or without handing off. Start the same kind of worker again

flag.title: One thing a shell flagged: what to do about it
flag.instructions: `note` is one thing a worker agent in a software pipeline flagged, beside its main result. `stage` says who wrote it and what happens next. Before the next step starts, what should the pipeline's driver do about the note?

choices.no: Nothing. The next step can start as it is
choices.note: Write it down where the next worker will read it (on the ticket or the pull request), then start the next step
choices.blocks: Do not start the next step. A person has to settle this first

ruling.title: A comment on a decision ticket: does it decide the ask
ruling.instructions: `ask` is one thing an issue asks its owner to decide. `comment` is a comment the owner left on that issue. Does the comment decide what `ask` asks?

choices.decides: Yes: the comment gives an answer to all of what `ask` asks
choices.open: No: the comment leaves some or all of what `ask` asks without an answer

same_defect.title: A defect just seen: is it the one this issue reports
same_defect.instructions: `seen` is a defect an agent just ran into in a tool. `filed` is the title of an issue already filed against that tool. Is `seen` the defect that `filed` reports?

choices.same: The same defect: add a note to the filed issue
choices.different: A different defect: the filed issue does not cover it

gate.title: A pull request before review: start the reviewer, wait, or send it back
gate.instructions: `pr` is what a tool printed about a pull request that a reviewer agent is about to check. What should the pipeline do now?

choices.wait: Wait: the pull request is not settled yet. Read it again later
choices.repair: Send it back to a builder: it conflicts with its base, or a required check failed

cases.source: reviewer's report, operator run on #556

texts.note:
Both come from reading the code, not from running it, and neither is one of the issue's three race bugs.
- https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/567: a child stopped with `child.run.stop()` keeps its scope open, so it stays in the host's table and the parent gets no notice. The `spawn` TSDoc and the how-to say "the table never holds a child that is not running" without that limit.
- https://github.com/kamp-us/demlik/issues/568: `SpawnSteps.notify` runs under `Effect.forkDetach` and accepts any error type, so a failing notify (a `StoreFailed` from `tell`) is seen by nobody. The TSDoc does not say so.

cases.source: issue's open question and the ruling comment, lane #601

texts.ask: Does this issue also ship a helper that walks a package's export map and returns the subpaths that publish a name? The filer asked for it as optional. The hard part is finding each subpath's source file: tea's export map points at `dist/`, and only `tsup.config.ts` knows that `./testing` comes from `src/testing/index.ts`. The options are (a) no helper: callers loop over their own subpath-to-source map and call the module query, (b) a helper that takes that map from the caller, (c) a helper that guesses `dist/X.js` -> `src/X.ts`.
texts.comment: Ruling (2026-10-10): **(b)**. Ship a helper that takes the caller's subpath-to-source map and returns which subpaths publish a name, with file:line. No layout guessing (`dist/X.js` -> `src/X.ts`) in the published API.

cases.note: No operator judged this one: the builder built option (b) from it.
